text: A refrigerator is a closed loop. One refrigerant travels round and round, picking up heat inside and dumping it outside.
The compressor squeezes cool, low-pressure vapor into a hot, high-pressure gas, like a bike pump warming up as you push.
In the condenser, the gas is hotter than the room, so heat flows out. It cools and condenses into a liquid.
The liquid is forced through a narrow expansion valve. Pressure drops suddenly, and its temperature plunges below freezing.
Now colder than the food, it absorbs heat in the evaporator and boils back into vapor, ready for the compressor again.
